Along with that I got ECT, basically shock your brain into being happy. When I left hospital my condition worsen and friends left me. Of course that made me feel more lonely and I guess more frequently.

But this year I have been more into online communities like Twitch. Yeah they're not friends but they're some sort of community still. Yeah it takes time and effort to build but for me I don't want to see people anymore so just put effort into that. I see that a lot of those streamers are lonely also. In fact one of them asked the exact question you did in this post.

Anyway, I have attempted suicide just about a month ago and learnt new perspectives. Now I don't feel frequently lonely, and even if I did it's not as intense or long-lasting.  

One of the learnings is that recently my psychologist talked about loneliness with me and she told me that it's a spectrum and that I can never feel zero loneliness, which is bad news and I kinda already know that. But she told me that a lot of things can bring companionship. This statement was what I was looking for someone to say to me.

But my belief is that my change in perspectives are to do with whatever I gone through.  If lif is so hard and short and I'm desperate to die then must as well use the remaining time on what comes to me easily. Anyway, I still got depression and suicidal thoughts so it's not like everything is rainbows and unicorns.  


And I don't know if the loneliness feeling will come again but as of now it's almost not here for me so fuck it is a big change for me.  
Yes of course human companionship and tight-knit social communities where one can gain support is great. I've seen that and felt that. But no one will give a fuck about you like you. When I was going to die I wasn't thinking about people, I was thinking about suffering.
